discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: van der Waals heterostructures and moire quantum materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands nearly flat, so electron-electron interactions dominate. In 2018, Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this experimentally. Using precisely controlled tear-and-stack fabrication of clean, hBN-encapsulated devices, they observed correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity that can be switched on and off with a gate voltage. This showed that the twist angle is a new, tunable knob for designing quantum phases in a single device. The work founded 'twistronics' and moire materials as a field. Laboratories worldwide have since found orbital ferromagnetism, Chern insulators, strange-metal transport and fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in moire systems. Few discoveries in recent decades have changed so quickly how experimental condensed-matter physicists build and study strongly correlated matter.
